title: Investigating entanglement dynamics with dynamical decoupling together with initial qubit-reservoir correlations
authors: Rifzah Shahid, Amna Qadeer, Ali Raza Mirza
abstract: We study the exact entanglement dynamics of two qubits coupled to a common bosonic reservoir through a pure dephasing interaction. We ask how this dynamics changes when the qubits and the reservoir already share correlations before the qubit state is prepared. In that case the system and reservoir first interact for a long time and settle into a joint equilibrium state. Only afterward is the qubit pair projected onto the desired state by a local measurement. For an Ohmic spectral density we obtain the exact reduced two qubit dynamics. Using the Wootters concurrence we show that initial correlations always speed up entanglement sudden death relative to the factorized case, and that this gap grows quadratically with the coupling strength in the weak-to-moderate coupling regime. Finally we show that a symmetric sequence of periodic π pulses applied to both qubits extends the entanglement lifetime close to a factor of seven over the range of pulse numbers studied.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes the entanglement decay of two qubits coupled to a common bath, focusing on the impact of initial correlations. It demonstrates that these correlations hasten entanglement sudden death, while applying periodic $\pi$ pulses can significantly extend the entanglement lifetime. The findings are important for understanding decoherence mitigation in open quantum systems.
main_problem: The study investigates how initial correlations between qubits and a common bosonic reservoir affect the entanglement dynamics of two qubits subjected to pure dephasing.
main_result: Initial correlations are shown to always accelerate entanglement sudden death compared to the factorized case, and periodic $\pi$ pulses can extend the entanglement lifetime by a factor of up to seven.
method: The dynamics are calculated exactly for the reduced density matrix using the Ohmic spectral density, comparing factorized and correlated initial states.
model_or_system: The system consists of two qubits coupled symmetrically to a common bosonic reservoir via a pure dephasing interaction. The Hamiltonian structure allows for exact solvability.
key_observables: Wootters concurrence, Entanglement Sudden Death (ESD) time, and the time evolution of the reduced two-qubit density matrix.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($g$), reservoir spectral density (Ohmic), and the number of applied $\pi$ pulses ($N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an Ohmic spectral density and utilizes approximations for the gap growth and bath averaging.
figures_summary: Figures compare concurrence decay curves for factorized vs. correlated states, and demonstrate the extension of entanglement lifetime by applying periodic $\pi$ pulses.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the factorized case, then incorporating initial correlations, and finally applying periodic dynamical decoupling pulses to extend coherence.
why_interesting: This work provides quantitative insights into how non-Markovian effects and initial system-bath correlations modify fundamental quantum measures like entanglement, which is crucial for designing robust quantum protocols.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (Color Online) Temporal evolution of the Concur- rence C(t), quantifying two-qubit entanglement dynamics in an exactly solvable two-qubit spin-boson model interacting with a common Ohmic bath for the factorized (dashed) and correlated (solid) Bell-state preparations. Chosen set of pa- rameters are ω0 = 1, ωc = 10, g = 0.25, T = 5.

FIG. 3. (Color Online) Concurrence C(t) for the factor- ized (dashed) and correlated (solid) Bell-state preparations at three qubit-reservoir coupling strengths, g = 0.1 (red), 0.05 (green), 0.025(blue), with T = 1.5, ω0 = 1.0, ωc = 10.0. Stronger coupling accelerates the decay of Γ(t) and hence of the entanglement envelope; the correlated curves again track the factorized ones very closely at these moderate couplings.

FIG. 2. (Color Online) Concurrence C(t) for the factor- ized (dashed) and correlated (solid) Bell-state preparations at three temperatures, T = 0.5 (red), 1.0 (green), 3.0(blue), with g = 0.1, ω0 = 1.0, ωc = 10.0. Higher temperature accel- erates the loss of entanglement through coth(βω/2) in Γ(t); at this coupling the correlated and factorized curves are barely distinguishable, consistent with the bound Ccorr(t) ≤Cunc(t).

FIG. 4. (Color Online) Concurrence C(t) without pulses (N = 0, dotted) and under periodic π-pulse control (solid), for the correlated Bell-state preparations with g = 0.1, ω0 = 1, ωc = 10, T = 2.0. Free evolution loses all entanglement by t ≈2–4, while the pulse-protected concurrence survives out to t ≈9–10: an extension of the entanglement lifetime by roughly a factor of four over this window.

FIG. 5. (Color Online) Entanglement death time tdeath, de- ﬁned as the ﬁrst time the concurrence falls below the numeri- cal threshold C(t) < 10−3, as a function of the (even) number of pulses N ∈{0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, for the factorized and corre- lated preparations (overlapping), at g = 0.15, ω0 = ωc = 1.0, T = 5.0. tdeath grows monotonically with N, from tdeath ≈1.7 at N = 0 to tdeath ≈11.9 at N = 10, delivering close to a seven-fold extension of the entanglement lifetime over the range of pulse numbers studied.
